title: Physics and defense technology
competency: Explain how radar, missiles and infrared night vision use physics.

keywords.def: RAdio Detection And Ranging: finding objects by the echoes of radio waves.
Electromagnetic radiation just beyond red light, given off by warm objects.

en.text: Radar sends out radio waves and times the echo. The wave goes to the target and back, so 2R = ct and the range is R = ct/2. A ballistic missile is powered only at the start and then follows a projectile path; a cruise missile is powered all the way. Infrared night vision shows warm objects as bright, because hotter objects give off more infrared.

screens.title: Echo timing
screens.ask: A radar pulse returns 0.0002 s after it was sent. The plane is
screens.after: The wave travels there and back: 3 × 10⁸ × 0.0002 = 60 km in total, so the plane is 30 km away.

screens.title: Radar
paras: RADAR means RAdio Detection And Ranging.
A transmitter sends a signal; the target reflects an echo back to the receiver.
The signal travels 2R in time t at speed c: 2R = ct, so R = ct/2.

screens.title: Radar range
screens.ask: Move the echo time. See the range.
screens.note: R = ct/2. The 2 is because the wave goes there and back.

screens.title: Missiles and night vision
paras: Ballistic missiles are rocket-powered only at the start, then move under gravity in an arc (Newtonian mechanics).
Cruise missiles are jet-powered all the way.
All objects give off infrared; hotter objects give off more. Night-vision devices show hotter objects brighter.
